findings.title: Empty error after sanitizing gives blank error
findings.problem: An error query value made only of control characters sanitizes to an empty string; OAuthCallbackError is then built with an empty oauthError and the page and message ('OAuth error: ') show nothing. Only the description is guarded with || undefined.
findings.impact: Trigger is a malformed or hostile error parameter; the user sees a blank failure reason. No behavior consequence beyond a less readable message.

findings.title: sanitize leaves line separators and bidi controls
findings.problem: sanitize strips only C0/C1 control characters. U+2028/U+2029 and bidi override or isolate characters (U+202A-202E, U+2066-2069) in the untrusted error and error_description reach the thrown message, stderr/logs and the page.
findings.impact: Trigger needs a hostile or compromised authorization server or local caller to craft the parameters; effect is log-line spoofing, not code execution. The page itself is HTML-escaped. Reachability read: the parameters are attacker-influenced query values.
findings.recommendation: Extend the character class to also remove \u2028\u2029\u200e\u200f\u202a-\u202e\u2066-\u2069.

findings.title: First-refusal path forgets login too eagerly
findings.problem: When the first refresh is refused and nothing newer is persisted, renewSilently deletes the persisted login via unconditional forgetPersistedLogin, for any OAuthError code including server_error. The retry path instead uses GRANT_ENDING_CODES and forgetPersistedLoginIf, and the doc comment says server errors may be transient and keep the grant. A sibling that persists a rotated login between the peek and the unlink would also lose its file.
findings.impact: Trigger is a transient OAuth-shaped server_error from the token endpoint, or a sibling write inside the very short peek-to-unlink window; the user must log in again in the browser. The spec says unchanged/absent persisted token keeps the existing forget behavior, so this is hardening, and a test currently locks in the deletion.
findings.recommendation: Apply the retry path's rule: gate on GRANT_ENDING_CODES.has(error.code) and call forgetPersistedLoginIf(this.serverUrl, grant.refreshToken); update the 'forgets on any OAuthError code' test accordingly.

findings.title: Provider-to-lock timing wiring is untested
findings.problem: redirectToAuthorization passes lockMaxWaitMs and lockStaleMs from getMcpAuthTimings() to acquireAuthLock, but no test asserts that wiring: lock tests use literal options and timing tests check only the pure function.
findings.impact: Swapping or dropping the options would keep all tests green and break the 0.75T / 1.25T invariant; no behavior consequence today.
findings.recommendation: Add a provider-level test: set MCP_PROXY_AUTH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=10, call redirectToAuthorization, read mcp-auth.lock and assert staleAfterMs === 12500.

deferred.title: Callback does not verify OAuth state
deferred.problem: /callback resolves with a code or rejects on error= without any state check; the provider implements no state(), so a local page or process can abort or inject into a pending login.
deferred.preexisting: state was already read and dropped, and no state() existed, before this change; PKCE limits injected codes.
